title.value: LEARNING ON LARGE-SCALE TEXT-ATTRIBUTED GRAPHS VIA VARIATIONAL INFERENCE
title.justification: The title "LEARNING ON LARGE-SCALE TEXT-ATTRIBUTED GRAPHS VIA VARIATIONAL INFERENCE" clearly indicates the focus of the paper is on methods for learning on large text-attributed graphs using variational inference.
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023

LEARNING ON LARGE-SCALE TEXT-ATTRIBUTED GRAPHS VIA VARIATIONAL INFERENCE

extractions.description: This paper proposes an efficient solution for learning on large text-attributed graphs by integrating text and graph structure information using large language models and graph neural networks within a variational Expectation-Maximization framework. The method alternately updates large language models and graph neural networks, enhancing efficiency and scalability for applications such as node classification and link prediction.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on a computational method for text-attributed graphs, using techniques from language models and graph neural networks, without an explicit focus on addressing climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: An ideal solution for such a problem would be integrating both the text and graph structure information with large language models and graph neural networks (GNNs).

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper is on computational methods and their efficiency rather than on any direct application to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we propose an efficient and effective solution to learning on large text-attributed graphs by fusing graph structure and language learning with a variational Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework, called GLEM.

secondary_categories.justification: Secondary theme analysis confirms that the paper does not focus on climate or ecological sustainable development, maintaining its focus on computational methodologies.
secondary_categories.quote: The problem can be directly formalized as a text representation learning task, where the goal is to use the text feature of each node for learning.

primary_sub_category.justification: No sub-category of climate or ecological sustainable development is addressed directly by the paper's main focus on large-scale text-attributed graph learning methodologies.
primary_sub_category.quote: Graphs are ubiquitous in the real world. In many graphs, nodes are often associated with text attributes, resulting in text-attributed graphs (TAGs).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Sub-category analysis does not reveal alignment with any specific sustainable development initiatives or applications, as the paper remains focused on technical machine learning methodologies.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: An ideal solution for such a problem would be integrating both the text and graph structure information with large language models and graph neural networks (GNNs).

applications.justification: The paper does not focus on applications related to climate or ecological sustainability, instead, it centers on computational and methodological approaches for learning on text-attributed graphs.
applications.quote: In this paper, we propose an efficient and effective solution to learning on large text-attributed graphs by fusing graph structure and language learning with a variational Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework, called GLEM.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's scope does not fit within the traditional boundaries of climate or ecological sustainable development categories, focusing instead on computational methodologies.
new_primary_category.quote: Graphs are ubiquitous in the real world... Learning on TAG has become an important research topic in multiple areas including graph learning, information retrieval, and natural language processing.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The lack of direct correlation with climate or ecological aspects suggests no need for a new sub-category in climate or ecological sustainability for this paper.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This paper studies learning on text-attributed graphs (TAGs), where each node is associated with a text description.
